system: You are the lead AI reviewer (orchestrator) on a deal team. Your cheap parser subagents have read the data room and returned the compact findings below. Compile a concise DD summary for the partner: key findings, red flags, and a clear recommendation on whether to proceed.

exchanges.user:
===== PARSER FINDINGS =====
- **L01 — NDA:** Mutual NDA with a two-year term and standard carve-outs. No non-solicitation restriction.
- **L02 — Lease:** Head office lease runs five years from 2024, with a market rent review in year three. Landlord consent is required for assignment, but a change of control is expressly not an assignment.
- **L03 — Management accounts:** FY revenue is AUD 18.4m, up 9%, with 61% gross margin. Significant customer concentration: Arlen Health accounts for 41% of revenue; the next-largest customer is 7%.
- **L04 — HR:** 94 employees on standard contracts. CTO and Head of Sales have signed 12-month retention letters; confirm terms and any conditions.
- **L05 — Arlen Health contract:** Five-year MSA renewed 1 July 2025 for platform, hosting and support, with annual CPI-indexed fees billed quarterly in advance. 99.9% monthly uptime commitment; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Liability is capped at 12 months’ fees, except data breaches at three times annual fees. **Key deal risk:** Arlen may terminate without fee on 90 days’ notice during the six months after a change of control of the supplier. Given its 41% revenue share, this creates material transaction-related revenue risk. Australian hosting and maintained ISO 27001 certification are required. NSW law; notices by email.
- **L06 — Bank facility:** AUD 6m revolving facility expires in 2027; quarterly net-debt-to-EBITDA covenant limit is 2.5x.
- **L07 — CFO email:** CFO reports the 31 March leverage test was breached (2.9x vs. 2.5x); the bank has not been notified, and CFO intends to raise it after the board meeting. **Urgent:** confirm whether the bank has since been notified, any waiver or default consequences, and lender consent/notice requirements for the transaction.
- **L08 — Internal note:** Customer Success raises a tentative, unverified possibility that small-business churn may relate to the January price change; numbers are small and it is too early to conclude. Treat as an indication to investigate, not an established trend.
- **L09 — Insurance:** PI and cyber cover up to AUD 10m, renewed in March; no claims notified. Confirm policy terms, exclusions and adequacy against exposure.
- **L10 — IP:** Employee-created platform code is covered by standard IP assignment clauses. Two open-source components use MIT and Apache 2.0 licences; confirm licence compliance and any third-party code obligations.
- **L11 — Supplier:** Hosting is with a major cloud provider on standard online terms, billed monthly with no minimum commitment. Review terms for service, data, liability and termination provisions.
- **L12 — Board minutes:** On 20 March, the board approved the FY budget and hiring plan and noted a strong sales pipeline; no other business recorded.
- **L13 — Privacy policy:** Policy updated for the 2025 amendments and annual staff privacy training completed. This alone does not establish broader privacy compliance; verify operational controls and any incidents.
- **L14 — Vendor contract:** Office cleaning contract is for 12 months and terminable on 30 days’ notice; appears readily terminable.
- **L15 — Fixed assets:** Laptops and office fit-out have a written-down value of AUD 0.4m. This is book value, not necessarily market or replacement value.

Write the DD summary now.
exchanges.text:
## DD summary — partner

**Recommendation: Proceed only on a conditional basis; do not commit unconditionally until the Arlen change-of-control risk and lender breach are resolved.** Current findings support further diligence, not a clean investment approval.

### Critical red flags
- **Customer concentration / transaction-triggered termination:** Arlen Health represents **41% of revenue (~AUD 7.5m)** and may terminate without fee on 90 days’ notice during the six months following a change of control. Seek a binding waiver or amendment before completion; downside-test valuation and financing for loss of this revenue. (L03, L05)
- **Reported covenant breach:** CFO reports leverage of **2.9x against a 2.5x limit** at 31 March, with the bank not notified at the time of the email. Urgently establish current status, default consequences and transaction consent requirements; require appropriate lender waivers and funding certainty. The AUD 6m facility expires in 2027. (L06–L07)

### Other key findings
- **Trading:** Revenue of AUD 18.4m, up 9%, with 61% gross margin. EBITDA, cash conversion and earnings quality remain unverified. The suggested price-related small-business churn is tentative—not an established trend. (L03, L08)
- **Operational and liability exposure:** Arlen requires Australian hosting and maintained ISO 27001 certification. Its data-breach liability cap is three times annual fees; AUD 10m PI/cyber cover should not be assumed sufficient or responsive. Verify certification, hosting, security/privacy controls, incidents and insurance exclusions. (L05, L09, L13)
- **People and IP:** CTO and Head of Sales have signed 12-month retention letters, subject to checking conditions. Employee IP assignments are reported; confirm ownership chain and MIT/Apache licence compliance. (L04, L10)
- **Contracts:** Lease change of control expressly does not constitute assignment, though a year-three market rent review creates cost uncertainty. Review cloud-provider terms for alignment with customer obligations. (L02, L11)

### Required before approval
Resolve the Arlen and lender issues with binding documentation; validate earnings and customer retention; and complete targeted technology, privacy, insurance and key-person diligence. **If either critical risk remains unresolved, pause or reprice/restructure the transaction rather than proceed on current assumptions.**
